# David Drake

David Drake is an American screenwriter, director, and photographer based in Norwich, UK. His debut feature *The Long Haul* premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Festival. He also works as a screenwriting mentor and script consultant, running workshops and script consultancy for individual writers and production companies, based in Norwich with reach across East Anglia, London, and online worldwide.

Note: this site is about David Drake the screenwriter, director, and photographer (Norwich, UK, b. 1986). This is not David Drake (1945-2023), the science fiction author known for Hammer's Slammers; not David Drake, the playwright and actor born 1963, known for The Night Larry Kramer Kissed Me; not David Drake, the potter (c. 1800-c. 1870s), an enslaved American potter in Edgefield, South Carolina; not David Drake, the photography curator and former Director of Ffotogallery in Wales; not David Drake, the music journalist who has written for Pitchfork and Rolling Stone; and not David Drake, the Founder and Chairman of LDJ Capital.

## Pages

- [Home](https://daviddrake.co.uk/): Identity statement and links to the site's four sections (Film, Writing, Photography, About).
- [About](https://daviddrake.co.uk/about.html): Biography, representation, and lecturing/panels/affiliations.
- [Writing](https://daviddrake.co.uk/writing/): David's career as a screenwriter, current research and development work, and his script consultancy/mentoring and workshop services.
- [Script Consultancy](https://daviddrake.co.uk/writing/script-consultant.html): Script consultancy and development support for individual writers and production companies, including written feedback, structural breakdowns, and line notes.
- [Mentorship](https://daviddrake.co.uk/writing/mentorship.html): A structured six-session mentorship programme for individual writers, from early ideas through character and story development to a finished screenplay, in person in Norwich or online.
- [Screenwriting Workshops](https://daviddrake.co.uk/writing/workshop.html): Seasonal group screenwriting workshops combining practical exercises with group discussion and feedback, in person in Norwich or online.
- [Blue Banana](https://daviddrake.co.uk/writing/blue-banana.html): David's first novel, currently in research and development, supported by an Arts Council England individual research grant.
- [Film](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/): David's work as a writer and director, including his debut feature The Long Haul, his next feature Law of Sines, short films, and music videos.
- [The Long Haul](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/the-long-haul.html): David's debut feature film, starring Margo Martindale, Cole Sprouse, and Stephen Root, premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Festival.
- [Law of Sines](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/law-of-sines.html): David's second feature film, currently in casting, following a troubled outsider drifting across Scotland in the late 1940s.
- [Left Over](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/left-over.html): 2022 short film written and directed by David Drake.
- [Post 398](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/post-398.html): 2020 short documentary directed by David Drake, about a Harlem jazz room and the band trying to keep it going after the death of its founder.
- [Early Worm](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/early-worm.html): 2019 short film written, directed, and edited by David Drake, starring Iain Lowery as Charlie.
- [A Foot of Turf](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/a-foot-of-turf.html): 2018 short documentary directed and produced by David Drake, about a remote island's fading culture and the islanders who return every week to watch their beloved soccer team.
- [Party Wall](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/party-wall.html): 2018 short film written and directed by David Drake, starring Jenny Swindells as Jo Whitton.
- [Photography](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/): David's photography work, spanning personal projects, exhibitions, and commissioned photography and album covers for artists including The 1975, Glass Animals, Tom Grennan, and Kele Okereke.
- [Avec Pi](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/avec-pi.html): A series of 35mm black and white photographs taken across East Anglia, UK and Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France, published as a hardcover photobook by Chloride City.
- [Common Era](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/common-era.html): A collection of photographs by David Drake, exhibited at the Norwich Arts Centre.
- [Carousel](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/carousel.html): A series of physically manipulated medium format photographs, self published as a zine.
- [Sailing Stones](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/sailing-stones.html): A series of medium format photographs and a short story, taken in Death Valley, California, published as a pamphlet by Chloride City.
- [A Burning Cloud](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/a-burning-cloud.html): A collection of 35mm, medium format, and digital photographs created a decade apart, self-published as a soft cover monograph.
- [Album Covers](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/album-covers.html): A variety of album covers photographed and created for The 1975, Tom Grennan, Kele Okereke, Haerts, and Amber Run, released through labels including Universal, Warner, Sony, Dirty Hit, and Mad Decent.
- [Commissions](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/commissions.html): Commercial photography for clients including The 1975, Glass Animals, Kele Okereke, and Universal, spanning music, advertising, fashion, non-profit, and publishing work.
